successors.name: French Africa
successors.text: Saloum with the Gambian north bank

ledger.x: c. 1494: Saloum is founded. "In the later part of the 15th century (c. 1494)" Mbegane Ndour, who came from Sine, founded it (Serer oral tradition); the page adds that Saloum existed in some form before him and "it is unclear what form it took".
By 1861-1862: Maba Diakhou Bâ takes Rip and most of Saloum.
ledger.cp: Maba Diakhou Ba (Almamy of Baddibu and Saloum)

ledger.x: 18 July 1867: Maba is defeated and killed.
ledger.cp: Maba Diakhou Ba (Almamy of Baddibu and Saloum)

ledger.x: 1867: Saloum is incorporated into the Senegal colony.

wars.name: Maba's jihad in Saloum
wars.outcome: Maba controlled Rip by 1861 and most of Saloum by 1862, was recognized by the French as Almamy of Baddibu and Saloum in October 1864, took the Battle of Pathé Badiane near Nioro on 30 November (1865), invaded Sine in 1866 and was defeated and killed at…

wars.name: French treaty of 1859 with Saloum
wars.outcome: Faidherbe's expedition "imposed a new treaty on the Maad Saloum" (the year is inferred from "two years later" after the 1857 Albreda exchange).

certainty.note: The page gives towns and regions but no outline; the Kaolack/Kaffrine regions are stand-ins and the Gambian north bank is drawn whole.
